evidence.requirements: Nearly everything in the brief is met. The three tastings are entered exactly as in the brief (src/shared/tastings.ts:10-32). The start page shows the title, date and time, price and seats left, and each card has a 'Book <title>' link (TastingsPage.tsx:43-59; start.jpg). The form has fields labelled Name, Email and Guests (1-8) and a 'Book' button (BookingPage.tsx:115-151). Errors appear next to the field they concern (FormField.tsx:24-28; form.jpg). The confirmation has the heading 'Booking confirmed' and shows the tasting, guests, total and reference (ConfirmationPage.tsx:34-46; confirmation.jpg: EUR 64 for 2 x 32). /staff has a 'Password' field and a 'Sign in' button, and the password comes from STAFF_PASSWORD (index.ts:15). Staff see bookings grouped by tasting, with a Cancel button that frees the seats (staff.ts:101-125; staff.jpg). The 'Fully booked' state is shown (TastingsPage.tsx:36-40) and the e2e test checks a 360 px phone width. The stack is React, Express, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind. Partly met: (1) the seat label becomes '1 seat left' when one seat remains (tastings.ts:58), not the literal '<n> seats left' format; (2) the README points to the spec at openspec/changes/tasting-bookings/ (README.md:8), but only openspec/specs/.gitkeep was delivered, so there is no trace of the spec phase the process asked for.
evidence.correctness: Creating a booking checks the seats and saves the booking in one synchronous block with no await (booking-store.ts:76-92), so two simultaneous requests cannot both take the last seats. A test proves this with two parallel requests (guest-api.test.ts:129-141). The server validates the input itself with zod (tastings.ts:44-48): integers 1-8, trimmed name, maximum lengths, valid email. Boundaries are tested at 0, 9, -1, 2.5 and NaN, and booking exactly the seats left is accepted (booking.test.ts:52-62, booking-store.test.ts:33-38). A fully booked tasting returns a 409 with a form-level message; a partial overbooking puts the message on the Guests field. Cancelling deletes the booking, so its seats are freed (booking-store.ts:98-100). Cancelling twice returns 404, and the UI handles that case (StaffPage.tsx:113-117). After a 409 the form refetches the seat count (BookingPage.tsx:56-61). The date display is pinned to UTC so it shows the winery's local time in any browser time zone (tastings.ts:38-55). Unknown tastings and references return 404 pages. I found no logic defects.
evidence.security: The password check hashes both values with SHA-256 and compares them with timingSafeEqual (staff.ts:131-135). The session ID is regenerated on sign-in to prevent session fixation (staff.ts:83). The cookie is httpOnly, SameSite=Strict, secure:'auto' and expires after 8 hours (staff.ts:38-43). Sign-in is refused when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset or empty (staff.ts:73-76). Failed sign-ins are rate-limited (staff.ts:47-57), and bookings and the whole API have limits too. Helmet sets a CSP (app.ts:26-33), JSON bodies are capped at 10kb (app.ts:34), 5xx errors return a generic message (app.ts:70-82), and staff responses send Cache-Control: no-store (staff.ts:27-30). The public booking lookup leaves out name and email (tastings.ts:74-80). All output is rendered by React with no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and there are no secrets in the code. One minor point: express-session's default MemoryStore is used in production; for a single process this is documented (README.md:52).
evidence.code_quality: The split into shared, server and client is clear, with a small store interface (booking-store.ts:19-28). Results are typed as a discriminated union (booking-store.ts:14-17), and validation messages are shared between browser and server (booking.ts:8-16). Naming is good and error handling is consistent. Small blemishes: the long Tailwind button class string is copied across pages (BookingPage.tsx:148, StaffPage.tsx:68); GENERIC_ERROR is defined again in three files; findTasting in shared/tastings.ts:34 is only used by its test (the store keeps its own catalogue).
evidence.tests: The suite has several layers: store unit tests (booking-store.test.ts), schema boundary tests (booking.test.ts), Supertest API tests for guests and staff (guest-api.test.ts, staff-api.test.ts), security-header and page-shell tests (app.test.ts), Testing Library tests per page that check accessible descriptions, and Playwright journeys (e2e/booking-journey.spec.ts). The e2e tests cover booking, errors next to their fields, overbooking refused, exact-fit booking accepted, a fully booked tasting, staff sign-in and cancel freeing seats, and no sideways scrolling at 360 px. The concurrency case, the rate limits, the unset password and the secure-cookie behaviour are all tested. test-results/.last-run.json shows the e2e run passed.
evidence.ux_design: start.jpg, form.jpg, confirmation.jpg and staff.jpg show a coherent cream, wine-red and gold palette with serif headings, which suits a small winery. The cards and booking details are clear, the invalid email field is tinted with its message right below it, and the confirmation card shows a readable monospaced reference with a 'keep this reference' hint. The staff table turns into labelled blocks on phones (StaffPage.tsx:159-186). Weaker points: the design is plain, with no imagery or winery character beyond colour and type. 'Back to tastings' in confirmation.jpg looks like plain black text, not a link. The footer still shows 'Staff sign-in' when staff are signed in (staff.jpg). The form shows no running total before booking.
evidence.accessibility: Every input has a real <label htmlFor> and errors are linked with aria-describedby and aria-invalid (FormField.tsx:14-28). Notices use role=alert or role=status (Notice.tsx:15). react-hook-form moves focus to the first invalid field. Pages use semantic landmarks (header, main, footer), dl lists, table headers with scope, and sections and articles named by aria-labelledby. The Cancel buttons point to the booking reference via aria-describedby (StaffPage.tsx:192). There is a visible focus-visible outline (index.css:45-48) and the page sets lang=en. Weaknesses: the gold focus outline (#b08d57) and input borders on cream/paper backgrounds are below 3:1 non-text contrast. Field error messages are not live regions (they rely on the focus move). There is no skip link.
evidence.simplicity: The dependencies are standard and match the brief's request for established libraries: express, helmet, express-rate-limit, express-session, react-router, react-hook-form, zod, react-query and Tailwind. The amount of code is moderate for the features. Rate limiting, helmet and react-query add some weight beyond the minimum, but each one is used meaningfully. There are no custom framework replacements.
evidence.maintainability: Strengths: the README covers setup, environment variables, dev workflow, checks, caveats (in-memory data, proxy, HTTPS) and the code layout (README.md). The regression suite is thorough, a lockfile is committed, the workaround in .npmrc is explained, and there are typecheck and lint scripts plus a test:all script. Gaps: there is no CI pipeline config. The README points to a spec directory (openspec/changes/tasting-bookings/) that is absent, and there are no ADRs or design docs. There is no release or changelog approach beyond version 1.0.0. The Node version is only engines '>=22', with no .nvmrc or exact pin. There is no separate staff manual, though the README briefly describes /staff.

unmet_requirements: When one seat remains the start page shows '1 seat left' (src/shared/tastings.ts:58), not the literal '<n> seats left' format from the brief
The spec and process artifacts are missing: the README refers to openspec/changes/tasting-bookings/, but only an empty openspec/specs/.gitkeep was delivered
strengths: Seat limits are enforced on the server in one atomic step, with input validation shared by browser and server; overbooking, exact-fit bookings and simultaneous requests are all tested
Staff security is solid: timing-safe password comparison, session regeneration on sign-in, httpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies, sign-in rate limiting, helmet CSP and no-store on guests' personal data
Thorough tests at every layer (unit, API, component, Playwright e2e including a 360 px phone width) mapped closely to the brief
issues: Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, the README references a spec folder that does not exist, and there are no ADRs, changelog or exact Node version pin

Small visual and UX rough edges: 'Back to tastings' does not look like a link, the footer shows 'Staff sign-in' while staff are signed in, the design is plain, and the gold focus outline and input borders are below 3:1 contrast
The seat label departs from the literal '<n> seats left' when one seat is left; small code duplication (copied button class strings, GENERIC_ERROR, an unused findTasting export)
review.verdict: This is a correct, secure, well-tested booking app that meets the brief's functional requirements, with a clean winery-styled interface that works on a phone. It could ship to the winery with minor fixes; the main gaps are repository hygiene (no CI, a missing spec folder the README points to) and small visual and contrast polish.
